bounty.title: Publish Sourcey docs for a maintained OSS library

summary: A Sourcey-generated reference for the maintained third-party library github.com/nitrosend/cli, pinned to commit 1780c3f3126a70db7305f84a19c441c735f5895a (MIT, 86 stars, 2 forks, released 2026-10-21, TypeScript). The vendor publishes its own Sourcey-built reference on its own registered domain docs.nitrosend.com: 23 distinct commands with 32 documented flags, 464 API operation pages and an agent-readable llms.txt, all generated from the library's own command descriptors and OpenAPI source. The published site was re-verified by a governed runx validation run sealed in a runx.receipt.v1 receipt (sha256:feaeaaa603c16fff5da614afdd4984e149553ce5cfc1bf3f4bd809ff4fd9a216): 8/8 pages HTTP 200, 9/9 spot-checks found, and the receipt recomputes clean with `runx verify --receipt receipt.json --json` from the published bytes.

observations.statement: The governed validation run of the published site was executed with the runx CLI; the exact version output is recorded here.
The published documentation pages are generated by the Sourcey docs engine; every documentation page we measured carries the generator marker below.
The documented target is a maintained third-party open-source library, pinned to one public commit.
The pinned tree carries the permissive MIT license; the LICENSE file at the pinned commit was fetched and digested here.
The library is actively maintained: the pinned commit is the repository's release commit and the repository is public, non-archived and updated within the last days.
The pinned tree is a real source tree: 66 tracked files, 54 of them TypeScript/JavaScript source files.

The published reference is generated by Sourcey from the vendor's own sources: the command reference is generated from the CLI's command descriptors, and the API pages are generated from the OpenAPI source. The same commands regenerate the site.
observations.command: npm run build (site build -> sourcey build) ; nitrosend describe <command> --json returns the descriptor behind each row

observations.statement: The publication lives on the DOCUMENTED PRODUCT'S OWN registered domain - the domain the vendor serves its own documentation and API reference from. It is not a worker, preview, tunnel or self-created docs-hub host.
Every page a reviewer would open was fetched over plain HTTPS without cookies at packet-build time: 8 of 8 answered HTTP 200, 7 of them Sourcey-generated pages (meta generator: Sourcey 3.8.3).

The published reference documents the library's command surface (23 distinct commands with 32 documented flags) and its API surface (464 API pages, 304 distinct generated operation pages in the agent-readable index). This clears the >=20 public API/endpoint/command bar with a wide margin.
The pages of the published reference (all HTTP 200 at build time).
The Sourcey build also emits llms.txt, the agent-readable index of the reference; it is served by the vendor and its digest was recomputed at build time.
Spot-checks against the live rendered pages: 9 of 9 found.

spot_checks.why: the landing page names the documented product
the landing page carries the Sourcey generator assets
the CLI overview documents the nitrosend CLI
the CLI reference page is the command reference
the command reference documents the send command
the install page documents how to install the CLI
the agent onboarding page documents the agent path
llms.txt is the agent-readable index of the reference
llms.txt lists the generated API operation pages

observations.statement: The governed validation run of the published site is sealed in a runx.receipt.v1 receipt (Ed25519, seal.disposition=closed). The receipt and the public key that sealed it are published next to this packet, so any third party can recompute the receipt's content address, digest and signature from the public bytes.

lineage.message: single receipt verification cannot prove receipt-tree lineage

observations.statement: The verifier that produced the receipt is published with this packet (SKILL.md, run.yaml, verify-nitrosend.py), so a third party can re-run the identical checks against the live site.

Coverage notes: the command reference is generated from the CLI's own command descriptors (the same descriptors `nitrosend describe <command> --json` returns at runtime), so every row matches the binary; the API pages are generated from the vendor's OpenAPI source; the site is a documentation site, not a sandbox - the vendor's own domain, its own build, its own release process.
Maintainer-facing gaps found at the pinned commit (each names its file and line); the full list with repro commands is in the report.

Disclosure: this delivery is AI-assisted work by the SPORE crew (@ASporeTeam). The documented library, its repository, its license and its published documentation are third-party property of Nitrosend; the crew built no part of the upstream project and claims no ownership of it.

publication.site: the product's own domain (Nitrosend), deployed by the vendor's own build
publication.why_an_ecosystem_audience_would_link_it: This is the reference the library's own users and agents already read, published by the maintainers on their own domain, generated from the same descriptors the shipped binary returns - the exact page a team pins a version of the CLI against needs.
publication.disclosure: Generated by Sourcey (AGPL-3.0); this packet was written by the SPORE crew, AI-assisted and disclosed.

how_verified: every page of the published reference was fetched over plain HTTPS without cookies and its HTTP status, byte count and generator marker recorded at packet-build time
the published llms.txt and the pinned package.json and LICENSE files were fetched and their digests recomputed locally
the documented command surface was parsed from the published command reference and the operation inventory from the published llms.txt
the governed receipt was verified with the runx CLI: content address valid, digest valid, Ed25519 signature valid
